blurb: Theory of equations: elimination, polynomial rings, Cardano and Ferrari, resultants, Galois theory and Newton's method.

pics.alt: A printed Latin page from Cardano's Ars Magna with a square diagram and the rule for solving a cubic
pics.caption: Chapter XII of Cardano's Ars Magna (Nuremberg, 1545), on the cube equal to things and a number (x³ = px + q): a geometric demonstration, then the rule. Its worked example x³ = 6x + 40 gives ∛(20 + √392) + ∛(20 − √392), which equals 4.
pics.title: Ars Magna Cardanische Formel.png

pics.alt: Pencil portrait of the young Évariste Galois
pics.caption: Évariste Galois (1811–1832) at about fifteen, in a drawing of c. 1826. Before his death at twenty he showed that an equation is solvable by radicals exactly when its group is solvable.
